rapport_notes: Jules is warm, empathetic ("Gosh, I'm so sorry about that"), and builds genuine connection; voice tone is friendly and patient throughout.
process_discipline_notes: Sheet 2 ("Meet Your Mover" / who's coming) was answered in Stage 1 as a direct response to customer concern, then repeated in Stage 2 when Jules said "a few days before you move to introduce you to your movers... who they are before they get there, we have this page on our website that kind of, has like a movers page bio." — this is a second mention of the same differentiator.

evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raised concern: "I've used move movers before but it kinda got screwed over a little bit." Jules responded: "But yeah, no problem. I can discuss everything that is included in the hour the rate and all of that." — acknowledged but did not dig deeper with follow-up questions like 'what specifically happened' or 'what would make you feel confident this time'; moved to data collection instead.

evidence_quotes.missing_close_lock: Call ends with 'thank you so much for choosing through us' and 'if you have any changes or updates, feel free to give us a call' — no explicit rate-lock statement or final ask for commitment.

top_strength: Jules nailed the quid pro quo framing and asked the agenda question before diving into logistics, establishing trust early and showing he was listening to the customer's prior bad experience.
coaching_note: When the customer raised a real concern (previous mover 'screwed her over'), Jules acknowledged it but didn't dig two layers deep—he pivoted straight to data collection instead of asking follow-ups like 'what specifically happened' or 'what would make you feel confident this time'; also, Sheet 1 (damage/carefulness) was never addressed anywhere in the call, and the close lacked an explicit rate-lock mention and final ask.
